- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) within 5 days, model overreacts to short-term volatility; apply downward bias of 2–4% for next 3 periods.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is > 85 and true outcome drops below 75, adjust downward by 5–10% for next 2 periods.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often misreads trend; use 2-period average of history + sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 0.7×history + 0.3×sentiment signal) for next forecast.
- Avoid forecasting beyond 30-day horizon unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.8) — otherwise, model tends to overfit recent noise.
